{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The lid gave on the third try, flakes of rust falling into the dirt like dried blood. Inside, wrapped in a square of oilcloth that had gone stiff and yellow, lay the things they had put there the summer he turned eleven: a jackknife with a chipped bone handle, a movie ticket stub, a photograph of the two of them on the porch steps squinting into the sun. And beneath those, folded small, the letter she had made him promise not to read until they were both old.

He was not old. He was forty-three. But she had not kept her end of things either, and he supposed that made them even.

"You found it," she said behind him. Her voice had the same low rasp it had always had, only more so, as if the years had sanded it down.

"You knew I would."

"I hoped."

He unfolded the paper. The handwriting was a child's, loops too big, the pencil pressed so hard it had nearly torn through. He read it once quickly and then again, slower, and the willow moved above him and the light kept going out of the sky.

When he finally stood and turned, she was smaller than he remembered, gray at the temples, one hand pressed flat against her side. She looked at the letter, then at him.

"Well," she said. "Was I right?"

Hollis folded the paper along its old creases and put it in his shirt pocket, over his heart, where she could not see him decide."}
